description: 'A 2030 Vision for European Offshore Wind Ports', published by WindEurope in May 2021 (authors Cecchinato, Ramírez and Fraile, edited by O'Sullivan), looks at what European ports must do to support the expansion of offshore wind. Coverage: European offshore wind capacity was expected to grow from about 25 GW to more than 110 GW by 2030, which needs ports for manufacturing, marshalling, installation and operation and maintenance. Content: the functions ports play across the project life cycle, the quay, storage and heavy-lift capacity they will need, investment needs and funding, the role of ports in hydrogen production and supply, and an annex of case studies of individual ports. Format and access: a report of about 44 pages on the WindEurope intelligence platform. Licence and cost: free to download; no licence stated. Caveats: an industry association view written to support investment, with figures from 2021. The capacity and investment framing can inform capacity planning and investment appraisal of port infrastructure where energy and maritime systems meet. It relates to the Associated British Ports adaptation report in the catalogue, whose ports serve offshore wind.
